newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Central Bank to tighten property loans.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Central Bank to tighten property loans.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes said on Wednesday the bank plans to impose stricter rules to curb the rise of loan exposure by banks to the booming real estate sector.

"We are looking at a probable reduction in loan value from the present 70 percent to say 50 or 60 percent," Reyes told Reuters in an interview, adding that the new rule might be in place by next quarter.
At present, banks are allowed to lend out 70 percent of the property's appraised value which in turn is 80 percent of the prevailing market value.
"If we reduce the loan value, it will take care of the growing size of the loan to the sector as well as give enough of a buffer for the bank if the prices go down," he said.

Exposure of Philippine banks to real estate developers and construction companies was estimated at $4.6 billion by the end of last year, or slightly above 10 percent of the total loan exposure of the commercial banking system. Real estate loans have been a small portion of bank loans in the past years.

Reyes said the move was not because banks have been over-extending their exposure in the property sector, but as a precautionary measure to prevent the Thailand experience where most of its banks ran into financial troubles due to the collapsing Thai property prices.
The reduction in loan value would not be imposed on low-cost homeowners and developers outside Manila.
Reyes also said it would change the reporting format of banks on their real estate exposure. At present, property loans were lumped together with loans to the financial institutions.

"We are going to segregate the real estate loans from the present setup. We are also going to ask them to give us the numbers by type of lenders, either homeowners or builders ... Then, it is easier to monitor," Reyes added.
